column1: # The errors a drawn case may raise (VARKA-319; VarkaExpectedErrors), after SQLancer.
# Tab separated: condition (or exception class), side (row, varka or both), modes (LEGACY and/or
# ANSI, comma separated), the coverage families that raise it (semicolon separated, or fixture),
# the reason. The Spark-level fuzzer treats a raise on this list, for that side and mode, as
# expected; any other condition is a finding. A listed condition raised by one engine only is still
# a disagreement. The families are documentation, checked against coverage.json but not used to
# decide: a listed condition is expected from any expression. The census behind the list is in plans/m7/VARKA-319.md 2.

column5: INT to INTERVAL DAY (d + CAST(i AS INTERVAL DAY)) is checked in every mode, and a hostile int (Int.MaxValue) overflows it. The fixture's year-month columns used to raise it too, whenever a hostile year was drawn, and now are NULL where the cast would overflow (VARKA-372), so the 5,000-composition runs meet it in four of seven seeds
Checked integer addition and multiplication raise on overflow under ANSI (i + 1 at Int.MaxValue); add_months(d, i) overflows under ANSI as well
add_months(d, i) adds the months with Math.addExact in every mode, so an int outside the date range raises even with ANSI off

x / x2 with a zero x2 (0.0 or -0.0) raises under ANSI: Varka's checked floating division sends a batch with a live zero divisor to the row engine, which raises it, as Spark's own division does. The fixture's x2 is a zero in three of its ten picks, so nearly every ANSI composition that draws the row meets it; with ANSI off, and under try_divide, the lane is NULL instead (VARKA-342)
make_date(2021, i, 1) with a month outside 1 to 12 raises under ANSI; with ANSI off it answers null

date_add(d, i) whose day sum leaves the int range raises a raw ArithmeticException (integer overflow) in every mode, which Spark reports wrapped in this condition; the wrapping is Spark's and the same on both engines
Year-month interval addition and subtraction (ym - ymm) use Math.addExact in every mode, so a result outside the int month count raises with ANSI off as well

Year-month interval construction and negation are checked in every mode: make_ym_interval(i, i) multiplies and adds the month count exactly, and d - ymm negates the interval, which overflows at an INTERVAL MONTH of Int.MinValue months (a hostile m); both engines raise it with ANSI off too. Met by the nested trees of VARKA-298, whose operands reach these positions with drawn ints
